sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Core Java is the gatekeeper of every Java fresher interview. Interviewers use these questions to separate candidates who understand the language from those who only copied code. A strong handle on OOP, exceptions, strings, and keyword semantics signals that you can reason about Java — not just write it.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Primitives vs Objects**: Java has 8 primitive types stored on the stack; everything else is an object on the heap.
- **OOP pillars**: **Encapsulation** (hide internals via access modifiers), **Inheritance** (IS-A reuse), **Polymorphism** (one interface, many forms), **Abstraction** (hide complexity behind contracts).
- **Strings are immutable**: Every modification creates a new object; use **StringBuilder** for mutable string work.
- **Exceptions are objects**: Checked exceptions must be declared or caught; unchecked (RuntimeException) do not.
- **static belongs to the class**: Not tied to any instance; **final** means no reassignment / no override / no subclass.
- **Access modifiers control visibility**: `private` < `default` < `protected` < `public` in widening order.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **java-syntax-datatypes**: Know all 8 primitives, their sizes, autoboxing pitfalls, and widening vs narrowing cast rules.
- **oop-fundamentals**: Be able to explain each OOP pillar with a one-sentence example; know method overriding rules.
- **exception-handling**: Distinguish checked vs unchecked; know finally always runs (except System.exit); explain try-with-resources.
- **string-basics**: Explain String pool, why String is immutable, when to use StringBuilder vs StringBuffer.
- **access-modifiers**: Know which modifier is default (package-private); know protected in inheritance context.
- **static-final-keywords**: Know static initializer block order; know final on a reference vs final on a primitive.
- **comparisons**: == compares references for objects; equals() compares content; know all 4 overloading vs overriding rules.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"Why is String immutable in Java?"* — Security (class loading), caching (String pool), thread safety — three reasons.
- *"What is the difference between == and equals()?"* — == is reference equality; equals() is logical/content equality.
- *"Can you override a static method?"* — No; static methods are class-level and hidden, not overridden (method hiding).
- *"What happens if you don't catch a checked exception?"* — Compile error; the compiler enforces declaration with throws.
- *"What is autoboxing and when can it cause problems?"* — Auto conversion between int↔Integer; can cause NullPointerException and performance overhead in tight loops.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"In Java, [concept] works by [mechanism], which means that [practical consequence] — and that's why [common interview implication]."*
